title: Hosted API demo - chat/text generation basics - Aperture Systems
summary: AE+SE walkthrough of Redwood hosted API for chat and text generation. Covered streaming responses, common request params (temperature, top_p, max_tokens), retry behavior, idempotency, and basic cost/latency tradeoffs. Customer asked about data retention, VPC/private options, and benchmarking. Agreed next steps: send pricing, security docs, and schedule a pilot/benchmark call.
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Morales: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we're gonna run through the hosted API demo today, quick intro then Priya will do a screen walk, mm-hmm
[00:18] Laura Chen: thanks Ethan, excited — we talked briefly with your sales team, I'm Laura CTO at Aperture, this is Mike and Rita from eng/ops
[00:30] Ethan Morales: awesome, quick agenda: show chat/text basics, streaming, key params, and how retries work in Redwood, and then Q&A; should be 30-ish minutes
[00:45] Priya Shah: sam e — i'll share my screen, can everyone see the console? there may be slight lag on the screen share
[01:05] Mike Alvarez: visible, yeah it's fine
[01:12] Priya Shah: perfect. so first quick note: hosted API is our fast path — single REST/SDK interface, supports chat, single-turn text generation, embeddings, reranking. i'm gonna demo a chat request hitting a tuned open model we host.
[01:35] Priya Shah: here's a simple chat call — payload includes messages array, model, and generation params like temperature, top_p, max_tokens, and stop sequences. we'll run with temperature 0.2 for focused responses then show higher temp for creativity.
[01:55] Mike Alvarez: do you support streaming? we stream tokens to our UI so latency matters
[02:02] Priya Shah: yep streaming is supported — server-sent events / chunked chunks over HTTP and SDK streaming. you'll see incremental tokens arrive; plus you can configure partial flush size.
[02:20] [Priya types, demo begins]
[02:32] Priya Shah: okay sending request now, you'll see the stream event come in, and each data chunk has a delta text piece and an index. note: transcription may show as data: [..] in the console
[02:50] Laura Chen: oh that looks pretty snappy, what's typical p95?
[02:57] Priya Shah: on hosted, p95 for short prompts is often sub-200ms for initial tokens on our fastest models but that depends on model choice, sequence length and context cache hits; warming helps.
[03:15] Mike Alvarez: context cache hits? you mean prefix cache or K V cache?
[03:21] Priya Shah: yeah kv cache / prefix caching — we cache common prefixes and K V layers to speed repeated convo turns. that's automatic on the runtime.
[03:35] Rita Gomez: we need to keep customer data in our cloud, so what's the default data retention on hosted?
[03:42] Ethan Morales: good question — hosted defaults to short retention for telemetry and request logs, full payloads can be disabled; for enterprise we offer dedicated and private modes with stricter retention and KMS options. i'll share the security docs after this call.
[03:58] Laura Chen: do you have SOC 2 or ISO?
[04:03] Ethan Morales: yes SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, plus SSO/SAML and RBAC. we'll include certs in the docs link.
[04:20] Priya Shah: back to streaming and params — here's an example toggling temperature to 0.8, you can see responses become more varied. top_p also affects nucleus sampling; lower top_p + low temp yields safe deterministic answers.
[04:45] [00:04:45 — small hiccup in audio, Priya repeats] 
[05:05] Priya Shah: another important thing: stop sequences and max_tokens — you should always set a reasonable max_tokens to bound cost and latency. if you expect short answers set max_tokens low, and use stop to avoid trailing artifacts.
[05:28] Mike Alvarez: what about retries? we get transient 5xx spikes from time to time and want idempotent behavior on retries
[05:34] Priya Shah: Redwood recommends using an idempotency key for non-streaming or n>1 calls. for streaming there's a connection-level retry strategy; we expose retryable error classes and backoff guidance in the SDK. by default we don't retry automatically for non-idempotent calls.
[05:55] Ethan Morales: and if you send the same idempotency key we will dedupe server-side so you won't double-charge for repeated attempts.
[06:10] Laura Chen: how granular are rate limits? we have bursts during business hours
[06:15] Ethan Morales: hosted has token-rate quotas per API key, and you can request higher tiers; for predictable bursts Dedicated gives reserved throughput. we can show the console quotas and per-token usage chart.
[06:35] Priya Shah: switching to the SDK snippet — here's a retry example: client.createChat({messages, model, idempotencyKey: 'abc-123', maxRetries: 3}) with exponential backoff. small note: if you stream, you may want to reconnect and resume from last token index rather than naive retry.
[06:58] Mike Alvarez: can we configure chunk size of streaming? sometimes we want more frequent small updates for typing UX
[07:05] Priya Shah: yes you can tune partial_flush_tokens and frequency on the runtime config — smaller flushes increase network overhead but improve perceived latency. that's one of the cost/latency levers.
[07:24] Rita Gomez: do you support custom stop sequences per tenant?
[07:28] Priya Shah: yup per-request stop arrays; also you can set model-level default stops in a deployment profile on dedicated/private setups.
[07:42] Laura Chen: and what's the best practice for multi-turn context? we have long conversations and care about cost
[07:48] Priya Shah: a few tips: use summarization or memory compaction to reduce context length; use prefix/KV caching for repeated system prompts; and occasionally offload long-term state to embeddings + DB then include relevant slices. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization and batching tweaks for cost savings.
[08:10] Ethan Morales: quick interjection, our Optimize product gives concrete estimates on token cost and suggests batching/caching configs per workload. we can run your sample trace in a pilot.
[08:25] Mike Alvarez: that would be useful — we want to compare cost to our current provider and measure latency regression risk
[08:32] Priya Shah: we also support A/B rollouts and model pinning so you can run canary traffic to Redwood without full cutover.
[08:45] [08:45 — slight cross talk] Mike Alvarez: good
[08:51] Priya Shah: security quick: for hosted, encryption in transit and at rest, optional customer-managed keys on dedicated/private, audit logs for every request, SSO, IP allowlists. you get per-route logging and cost attribution in the console.
[09:12] Laura Chen: can we get logs forwarded to our SIEM?
[09:17] Ethan Morales: yes log forwarding via secure syslog or S3, we also provide CloudTrail style exports for AWS integrations.
[09:28] Priya Shah: back to demo — i'm showing streaming with a multi-turn conversation. notice we send messages with role system/user/assistant, and on the server side the model uses the system prompt for behavior.
[09:48] Priya Shah: here's a failure scenario — i purposely disconnect the stream to show reconnection behavior. when the client reconnects with the same idempotency key and last-token index, the server resumes or returns the completed generation if it already finished.
[10:18] Mike Alvarez: cool. what's the typical number of tokens per second for generation? we care about throughput for batch scoring
[10:24] Priya Shah: depends on model / GPU. on our fastest configs you can see several hundred tokens/sec for batch workloads; for low latency it's smaller but pipelined. batching improves GPU utilization and lowers per-token cost for high throughput workloads.
[10:45] Laura Chen: is there an SDK for retries/streaming in our stack (python/ts)?
[10:50] Priya Shah: yes python and js SDKs with streaming helpers, reconnects, and built-in backoff strategies. examples are in the repo.
[11:05] Rita Gomez: question about credentials and rotating keys—we rotate keys from our side, how does Redwood handle revoked keys mid-request?
[11:12] Ethan Morales: if a key is revoked mid-request the connection will close with auth error; recommended pattern is issuing short-lived keys via a backend token exchange or use service credentials on dedicated/private. we'll include patterns in the security doc.
[11:30] Priya Shah: moving on to example payloads and cost control — set max_tokens, use stop and temperature, and if you need deterministic output set temperature 0 and top_p 0.8 or lower, but there's tradeoff.
[11:50] Mike Alvarez: curious about billing granularity — are we billed per-token including prompt and completion?
[11:55] Ethan Morales: yes per-token billing includes prompt+completion; we show breakdown in Console by route/model and token-type. you can also set per-route quotas to prevent runaway costs.
[12:15] Priya Shah: another pro-tip: for high-frequency short prompts, batching at the gateway reduces overhead. Redwood runtime does continuous batching when configured.
[12:30] Laura Chen: you mentioned model variants and fallbacks — how does that work?
[12:35] Priya Shah: policies can route by latency or cost; if primary model is unavailable we'll fallback to a cheaper compatible variant automatically. you can control fallback order and SLOs.
[12:50] Mike Alvarez: do you surface mismatch or quality regression alerts? we need to be warned when a model drift reduces QA pass rate
[12:57] Ethan Morales: yes Redwood has quality monitoring tied to evals; you can upload prompt sets and set regression thresholds, alerts go to the console and webhooks.
[13:12] [Priya scrolls through console showing evals tab]
[13:30] Priya Shah: wrapping up the demo, here's a sample code snippet showing streaming handler and reconnect logic. i'll paste the snippet in the chat after the call.
[13:45] Laura Chen: thanks, this is helpful. two immediate asks: 1) pricing and example cost for our workload, 2) security pack + SOC2 certs.
[13:56] Ethan Morales: noted. we'll send pricing and security docs. also propose a pilot: run a 2-week benchmark with your test set, Redwood Optimize team will run cost/latency analysis.
[14:10] Mike Alvarez: sounds good — who will own the pilot from Redwood?
[14:14] Ethan Morales: Priya will be the technical lead, and I'll coordinate commercial/pricing.
[14:22] Priya Shah: happy to run it. we can also do a deeper technical deep-dive on dedicated/private if you want to explore VPC options.
[14:32] Rita Gomez: we likely need VPC for PCI/PHI later, so yes let's schedule a security/deep-dive with infra team
[14:40] Ethan Morales: great — i'll send calendar invites for pilot kickoff and security deep dive.
[14:48] Laura Chen: any rough timeline for onboarding?
[14:51] Ethan Morales: hosted quickstart can be minutes to hours; pilot provisioning and dedicated/private timelines depend on contract, but pilot for benchmarks we can start next week pending PO.
[15:05] Priya Shah: final pointer: our SDK logs and metrics will help you tune partial flush and batching. i'll include a small checklist in the follow-up.
[15:18] Ethan Morales: ok wrapping — thanks for your time. we'll send pricing, security docs, SDK snippet, and proposed pilot plan. any final q's?
[15:28] Laura Chen: none for now — thanks all
[15:31] Mike Alvarez: thanks
[15:33] Rita Gomez: thanks
[15:35] Ethan Morales: thanks team, bye
